answer: A verifiable delay function mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to evaluate non-parallelizable sequential hash chains to maintain active status. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated single-thread execution time per identity. Whether an agent inspects a coastal jetty, evaluates a symbolic sonnet, or surveys a limestone karst, sequential operations cannot be parallelized. However, this continuous evaluation consumes excessive energy and penalizes resource-constrained nodes.
